diagnosis.summary: product-service is experiencing severe tail latency over the past 4 minutes, with p95 end-to-end latency at 1586 ms against a baseline of 6 ms. DynamoDB read throttling on the Products table is active, with 1400 read throttle events per minute recorded against a baseline of zero. The p50 latency and request rate remain near baseline, indicating the problem is concentrated at the tail.
diagnosis.root_cause: DynamoDB read throttling on the Products table is the most likely root cause, with read capacity consumed rising sharply and throttle events accumulating while request rate stays flat.
evidence: read_throttle_events jumped from 0 to 1400 count/min, confirming active DynamoDB read throttling on the Products table.
db_latency_ms_p95 rose from 4 ms to 1580 ms, a 395x increase, reflecting extended time spent inside DynamoDB calls at the 95th percentile.
p95_latency_ms rose from 6 ms to 1586 ms (a 264x increase) while p50_latency_ms moved only from 5 ms to 6 ms, showing the impact is entirely in the tail.
db_consumed_read_capacity surged from 480 to 11900 RCU/min, a 24.8x increase, while request_rate held flat at 15.1 rps versus a baseline of 15.0 rps.
error_rate_5xx rose from 0.0 to 0.004 (0.4%), indicating a small share of requests are exhausting all retry attempts.
recommended_actions: Raise the Products table provisioned read capacity or switch it to on-demand mode to immediately relieve throttling.
Investigate whether GET /products is performing full table scans on each call; introduce pagination with a limit and next-page token to reduce RCU consumption per request.
Add a product list cache inside the Lambda function to reduce repeated full-table reads across invocations.
After each change, recheck read_throttle_events and db_latency_ms_p95 to confirm throttling is subsiding.
Leave SDK retry settings unchanged during the incident to avoid converting current tail latency into additional 5xx errors.
